hints: Look carefully at the heights of the bars. P is by far the tallest at about 13 mm, S is next at about 4 to 5 mm, and Q and R are both very short at about 2 to 3 mm.
Remember the rule that muscle wall thickness matches the work done. Ventricles are much thicker than atria, and the chamber pumping furthest at highest pressure needs the thickest wall.
walkthrough:
**Rank the bars from thickest to thinnest**

Great start, let us just read the chart. P is thickest at about $13 \text{ mm}$. Next is S at about $4.5 \text{ mm}$. Then R at about $3 \text{ mm}$. Thinnest is Q at about $2 \text{ mm}$.

So the order is: P > S > R > Q.

**Link thickness to pumping job**

Here is the key biology idea. Thicker muscle means more force for higher pressure and longer distance.

Ventricles pump blood out of the heart, so they are much thicker than atria which only pump a short distance down into the ventricles.

**Assign each chamber**

The left ventricle pumps all round the body at high pressure, so it is the thickest. That must be P.

The right ventricle only pumps to the nearby lungs at lower pressure, so it is the next thickest. That must be S.

Of the two thin atria, the left atrium has slightly more work than the right atrium, so R is the left atrium and Q, the thinnest of all, is the right atrium. That matches row D.

options.A: Swaps the two atria. Q is thinner than R, so Q must be the right atrium and R the left atrium, not the other way round.
options.B: Gets P correct but swaps left atrium and right ventricle. S is too thick to be an atrium, it must be the right ventricle.
options.C: Swaps the ventricles. P at 13 mm is far too thick to be the right ventricle, it must be the left ventricle which pumps round the body.
options.D: Correct ranking: Q (thinnest) is right atrium, R is left atrium, S is right ventricle, P (thickest) is left ventricle.
